title: Manage Documents
description: Use the Codebeamer Document Manager to organize, version, and link supporting documents for the JAWS proof-of-concept project, and wrap up the course.

topics.title: The Document Manager

content.text: Alongside trackers, requirements, tests, and releases, every Codebeamer project includes a Document Manager. JAWS engineers use it to store reference material - specification documents, supplier files, and meeting notes - that supports the requirements and test items in the proof-of-concept project, without forcing that content into a tracker.

The Documents tab gives every project a shared file repository. JAWS can use it to centralize files that previously lived in shared drives or email attachments, scattered across their legacy ALM repositories - bringing those artifacts into the same traceable environment as their requirements and tests.

rows: Create a hierarchy to organize documents by topic, team, or document type
Upload single files or multiple files as a .zip, .tar, or .gzip archive; download multiple files as .zip
Lock a document for editing so other users cannot change it while you are working on it
Track every uploaded version of a document and prevent accidental overwrite or deletion
Add comments and related attachments directly on a document
Link a document to other work items, such as tasks, requirements, or test cases

content.text: The default maximum size for a single document upload in Codebeamer is 5 GB. Administrators can change this default in the Codebeamer configuration if larger files need to be stored.

For the JAWS proof-of-concept, the Document Manager gives engineers a way to keep supplier specification documents, test reports, and meeting notes alongside the requirements and tests they relate to - and to associate those documents directly with tracker items, so reviewers can move from a requirement to its supporting documentation in one click.
Always lock a document before downloading it to make changes. This prevents another team member from uploading a conflicting version while you are editing.

content.prompt: Match each Document Manager feature to what it provides:

pairs.right: Tracks every uploaded version and prevents accidental overwrite
Restricts other users from editing a document while you work on it
Links a document to a task, requirement, or other work item
Organizes documents into a hierarchy by topic or team

keyTakeaways: The Document Manager is a shared file repository available in every Codebeamer project, accessed from the Documents tab
Folders, version control, locking, comments, and associations help teams manage shared files alongside tracker data
Documents can be associated with tasks, requirements, or other work items for full traceability
The default maximum upload size for a single document is 5 GB, which administrators can adjust

topics.title: Document Versioning and Course Wrap-Up

content.text: Every time a document is re-uploaded to the same location in the Document Manager, Codebeamer creates a new version rather than discarding the old one. This version history gives JAWS a complete record of how a document changed over time - and a way to recover an earlier version if needed.

Each upload to a document increments its version number. The History tab on a document's properties shows every version, when it was uploaded, and who uploaded it. From there, any earlier version can be restored - which itself creates a new version, so the full history is always preserved. For example, if version 1 is restored after version 2 was uploaded, the document now has three versions: version 1 and version 3 are identical, and version 2 remains the version that was edited.
Restoring a previous version does not delete the versions in between - it adds a new version that copies the restored content. Version history in Codebeamer is additive, not destructive.

This module completes the Codebeamer Technical Essentials course. Across the previous modules, the JAWS proof-of-concept project demonstrated how Codebeamer supports the full ALM lifecycle: capturing and tracing requirements, defining and executing test cases, planning releases, analyzing project data through reports, and integrating with existing repositories. The Document Manager adds one more piece - a shared, version-controlled space for the supporting documents that accompany that work.

JAWS set out to replace its legacy ALM tools with a single platform covering requirements, tests, releases, reporting, integration, and document management. Each module of this course mapped to one of those needs - together they form the proof-of-concept that shows Codebeamer can support JAWS end to end.

content.prompt: Arrange the areas of the Codebeamer proof-of-concept in the order JAWS explored them across this course:

keyTakeaways: Re-uploading a document creates a new version; nothing is overwritten or lost
The History tab lists every version of a document and allows any version to be restored
Restoring an old version adds a new version rather than deleting the versions in between
The Document Manager completes the JAWS proof-of-concept by adding shared, version-controlled supporting documentation to the project

topics.title: Create a Directory and Upload a Document

content.text: In this exercise, you will create a folder structure in the Document Manager for your JAWS working files, upload a Word document into it, and edit and re-upload that document to see Codebeamer's version control in action.

You will need a Word document to upload, such as a copy of an Auto Requirements Document. If you do not have a remote desktop environment available, you can substitute any .docx file you have access to and edit it locally before re-uploading.

content.title: Create a Directory and Upload a Document
content.objective: Create a folder structure on the Documents tab, upload a Word file, then edit and re-upload it to create a new version.

steps.detail: The Documents tab opens the Document Manager for the current project, showing the folder tree in the left pane.

steps.action: In the left pane, ensure .codeBeamer is selected, click New on the toolbar, and then click Directory.
steps.detail: The .codeBeamer node is the root folder of the document repository. New directories are created beneath whichever folder is currently selected.
steps.hint: If New is greyed out, click directly on the .codeBeamer node first.

steps.action: In the Name box, type <your name> Documents, in the Description box type Directory for <your name> documents, and then click OK.
steps.detail: The description helps other JAWS team members understand the purpose of the folder when browsing the repository.

steps.action: With the <your name> Documents directory selected, repeat the steps to create a Word sub-directory, with the description Directory for my Word documents.
steps.detail: Sub-directories let you organize documents by file type, team, or topic - in this case, separating Word documents from other file types.

tasks.title: Upload, Edit, and Re-upload a Document

steps.action: With the Word directory selected in the left pane, click New, and then click File.
steps.detail: This opens the file upload dialog scoped to the currently selected folder.

steps.action: Click Choose files to upload, select your Auto Requirements Document.docx file, and then click Open, and then click Upload.
steps.detail: The file is uploaded as version 1 of the document and appears in the Word directory.

steps.action: Beside Auto Requirements Document.docx, click more, and then click Lock.
steps.detail: Locking the document prevents other users from uploading a conflicting version while you make your edits.
steps.hint: The lock icon appears next to the document once it is locked.

steps.action: Click more again, click Download, and save the file to your local machine, replacing the existing file if prompted.
steps.detail: Downloading gives you a local copy to edit. The locked status remains in Codebeamer while you work.

steps.action: Open the downloaded file in Word, add a new paragraph after the first paragraph with the text This is a new paragraph, then save and close the file.
steps.detail: This change will be visible when you compare the new version against the original after re-uploading.

image.alt: Auto Requirements Document.docx open in Word with a new paragraph added below the first paragraph
image.caption: The document with the new paragraph added

steps.action: In the Word directory, repeat the upload steps to re-upload the edited Auto Requirements Document.docx, replacing the existing file when prompted.
steps.detail: Re-uploading to the same location does not overwrite the original - it creates version 2 of the document.
steps.hint: Check the Version column or the document's History tab to confirm the version number increased.

keyTakeaways: Directories and sub-directories are created with New > Directory from the Documents tab
Locking a document before downloading it prevents conflicting edits from other users
Re-uploading an edited document to the same location creates a new version rather than replacing the file

topics.title: Link a Document and Restore a Version

content.text: In this exercise, you will link the document you uploaded to a task using an association, confirm the link from both sides, and then use the document's version history to restore an earlier version.
This exercise continues from the previous one. You should already have an Auto Requirements Document.docx with at least two versions in your Word directory.

content.title: Link a Document and Restore a Version
content.objective: Create a task, associate it with a document, verify the association from both the document and the task, and restore a previous document version.

tasks.title: Link the Document to a Task

steps.action: Navigate to the Tasks tracker and create a new task with Summary: Edit requirements document, Description: Task for the edit requirements document, and Assigned to: admin. Leave the remaining fields at their defaults, and click Save.
steps.detail: This task represents the work of editing the requirements document, and will become the target of the document's association.

steps.action: Click the Documents tab, and in the left pane click the Word directory.
steps.detail: This returns you to the directory containing Auto Requirements Document.docx.

steps.action: Beside Auto Requirements Document.docx, click more, then click Properties, and at the bottom click the Associations tab.
steps.detail: The Associations tab on a document's properties shows links between this document and other Codebeamer items.

steps.action: Click Add Association, in the Association Type list click is related to, then on the From History tab select the Edit requirements document check box and click Add.
steps.detail: This creates a bidirectional link - the document is now related to the task, and the task is related to the document.
steps.hint: The task should appear as the first item in the From History list if you created it just before this step.

image.alt: Document properties Associations tab showing 'is related to TASK-5782 Edit requirements document'
image.caption: The document associated with the task

tasks.title: Verify the Association and Restore a Version

steps.action: Navigate to the Tasks tracker, click Document View on the header toolbar, right-click the Edit requirements document item, and click Open.
steps.detail: Document View presents tracker items in a hierarchical layout, useful for reviewing one item at a time.

steps.action: At the bottom of the task, click the Associations tab and confirm that Auto Requirements Document.docx appears as a related item.
steps.detail: Seeing the association from the task confirms the link works in both directions - from document to task, and from task to document.

image.alt: Task Associations tab showing 'DOC-63348 Auto Requirements Documents.docx is related to this item'
image.caption: The task's Associations tab showing the related document

steps.action: Return to the Documents tab and the Word directory, beside Auto Requirements Document.docx click more, then click Properties, and click the History tab.
steps.detail: The History tab lists every version of the document, including the original upload and your edited re-upload.

steps.action: In the Version column beside version 1, click more, then click Restore this version, and click OK.
steps.detail: Restoring version 1 creates a new version (version 3) that is identical to version 1, while version 2 remains in the history as the edited version.
steps.hint: After restoring, the History tab should show three versions: 1, 2, and 3.

image.alt: Document History tab showing three versions, with version 3 restored from version 1
image.caption: The document's version history after restoring version 1

keyTakeaways: Associations are created from a document's Properties > Associations tab using Add Association
An association between a document and a task is visible from both the document and the task
Restoring a previous version from the History tab adds a new version rather than removing later versions
This exercise completes the JAWS proof-of-concept walkthrough across requirements, tests, releases, reporting, integration, and document management
